selection.rationale: The objective is peak_allocated_bytes for one batch-32 FP32 ResNet-18 forward (baseline 281,975,808 B; throughput floor images_per_second >= 7120.3, i.e. latency <= 4.4942 ms vs 4.2695 ms baseline). The measured peak is set by the stem: the eager ResNetConvLayer runs conv1 -> BatchNorm2d -> ReLU out-of-place, so during aten::batch_norm the conv1 output (32x64x112x112x4 = 102,760,448 B) and the BN output (another 102,760,448 B) are simultaneously live on top of resident weights (11,689,512x4 = 46,758,048 B) and the GPU-resident input (19,267,584 B) = 271.5 MB of the 282.0 MB observed peak (remainder consistent with conv workspace/maxpool int64 indices). I verified this subtree in the call tree: model.resnet.embedder (912.0 of 4163.5 us inclusive diagnostic CUDA, 5 kernels: conv1 268.0, BN 227.7, ReLU 216.1, maxpool 198.8 us). Every stem kernel is bandwidth-bound (~900 GB/s effective on the leased RTX 4090: BN moves ~205 MB/227.7 us, ReLU ~205 MB/216.1 us, maxpool ~180 MB/198.8 us), and the timeline shows the GPU nearly saturated (4093.7 us kernel union, only 74.1 us gaps) while host dispatch finishes ~2 ms early (cuda_synchronize self 2.11 ms of 4.50 ms profiled wall). Therefore restructuring only the stem keeps total memory traffic constant, so the throughput floor is protected, and the host has ample slack for a few extra chunked calls. All later activations are <= 25.69 MB per tensor, so after the stem fix the peak moves to the stage-0 residual moment (~46.76 weights + 19.27 pixels + 4x25.69 live = ~168.8 MB), which is the honest floor for a stem-only edit. The selected region is one coherent editable boundary: replace the whole bundle inside model.resnet.embedder (a single module-boundary direct callable replacement at the ResNetEmbeddings group), explicitly replacing the inner ResNetConvLayer/Conv2d/BatchNorm2d/ReLU/MaxPool2d module groups and their aten::conv2d/batch_norm/relu/max_pool2d functional calls, per binding-contract whole-bundle replacement. Model, pixels, workload, precision and evaluator are untouched.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing the stem bundle at the model.resnet.embedder boundary with a memory-lean equivalent that (a) processes the frozen batch through conv1->BN->ReLU->maxpool in 2-4 per-sample chunks (all four ops are strictly per-sample, so chunks are elementwise exact) and rejoins before stage 0, and/or (b) folds the frozen eval-mode BN affine into conv1 (scale/bias precomputed from the pinned running stats, warm-model and measurement boundaries unchanged) with an in-place ReLU, removes the simultaneous full-resolution 102.76 MB temporaries. Predicted peak_allocated_bytes drops from 281,975,808 to approximately 168-185 MB (-34% to -40%; with 2-chunk no-fold ~178 MB, with fold+in-place+2-chunk ~140 MB bounded below by the stage-0 moment ~168.8 MB plus conv workspaces); chunk workspace and the 51.38 MB maxpool int64 index tensor shrink proportionally too. Expected latency change is small (bandwidth-bound kernels with unchanged total bytes; extra launch overhead hidden by the 2 ms host slack and 224.7 us latency budget; a BN fold would additionally remove ~228 us of GPU time), keeping images_per_second >= 7120.3. Logits should remain within atol=rtol=1e-4 with exact top-1 (chunking is per-sample exact; BN folding only reorders rounding of the same FP32 arithmetic), to be verified by the frozen evaluator's repeated-forward closeness, exact-top1 and +1-corruption checks. If measurement shows cudnn picks a slower algorithm at the chunk batch size or the fold perturbs logits beyond tolerance, the chunk size / fold choice is retunable inside the same region without changing the boundary.

proposal.rationale: Single module-boundary replacement of the whole observed stem bundle at model.resnet.embedder (ResNetEmbeddings, call fa7ef6548e3a2d54174caeba). The frozen objective is peak_allocated_bytes for one offline batch-32 FP32 forward (baseline 281,975,808 B) with images_per_second >= 0.95 of baseline. The measured peak is set by the eager stem: during aten::batch_norm the conv1 output (32x64x112x112 fp32 = 102,760,448 B) and the BN output (another 102,760,448 B) are simultaneously live on top of resident weights (11,689,512 params = 46,758,048 B) and the GPU-resident pixels (19,267,584 B), with the maxpool 3x3 s2 int64 index buffer (51.38 MB at batch 32) and conv workspace making up the remainder. conv2d, eval-mode batch_norm (frozen running stats, training=False), relu and max_pool2d are all strictly per-sample operators, so the replacement streams the batch through the identical parent operators in fixed 8-sample chunks (4 chunks for the frozen batch 32; the remainder loop handles any other batch without changing the frozen workload) and copies each pooled chunk into one preallocated (32,64,56,56) output tensor returned to stage 0. No operator, dtype, batch, sequence, sampling, precision policy, TF32/cudnn setting, quality threshold or completion boundary changes: every chunk still executes the observed parent aten operators aten.conv2d (8504783bbca736066fecb204), aten.batch_norm (89bc7485bcb9aeaa62c7d28b), aten.relu (89f968d79a78e013c08bd56c) and aten.max_pool2d (4367176c34e4141fee648ee6) through context['references'], so the parent work executes on every invocation (4 reference invocations per site per forward, recorded in path telemetry), and no functional replacements are installed, so no dispatch-mode overhead or interception is added on any other operator in the project. Predicted warm-run peak: during a chunk only conv_out + bn_out (2 x 25.69 MB) plus the retained 25.69 MB output are live, so the stem moment drops from ~271.5 MB of live tensors to ~143 MB + small per-chunk conv workspace and 12.84 MB chunk index buffers; after the stem fix the invocation peak moves to the unchanged stage-0 residual moment (~46.76 weights + 19.27 pixels + 4 x 25.69 MB live activations ~ 168.8 MB), which is the honest floor for a stem-only edit per the selection analysis. Expected peak_allocated_bytes ~169-176 MB versus 281.98 MB (~38-40% lower), with the exact value to be measured by the paired evaluator. Latency: total stem bytes moved are unchanged for conv/BN/ReLU (same aggregate sizes), the only added traffic is 4 contiguous device-to-device copies of 6.42 MB each (~51 MB total) plus ~15 extra host launches, which the observed ~2 ms host dispatch slack and 224.7 us latency budget (floor 4.4942 ms vs 4.2695 ms baseline) absorb; GPU kernels remain the same bandwidth-bound families at the same aggregate sizes. No previous feedback exists (inputs/previous-feedback.txt absent and no inputs/previous-candidate), so this is the first attempt at the selected region; BN-folding into conv1 was deliberately not used because the stage-0 moment already bounds the peak after chunking, so folding would add rounding-reordering risk with no additional memory benefit; an in-place ReLU was likewise not used because the parent out-of-place aten.relu site is available through its reference and the stem moment is already below the stage-0 floor. Fallback discipline: build resolves the parent reference, the three physical modules (Conv2d a929588cc0791799075542c6, BatchNorm2d d2690ee924ab33cd95efa6f0, MaxPool2d 12da68be9b9e14502fe4702a) and the four operator references; if resolution fails the returned callable routes every call to the parent under the 'setup_failure_parent' route label; signature/attribute guards (CUDA fp32 4-D input matching in_channels, eval-mode affine track-stats BN, zeros padding, groups=1, no indices/ceil_mode pooling) route unsupported calls to the parent under 'unsupported_signature_parent'; a mid-computation operator exception routes to the parent under 'runtime_failure_parent'. The chosen chunked path self-reports 'chunked_stem_composite' via context['record_route'] invoked inside the replacement.
proposal.setup_work: build(context) performs no GPU work and allocates no device memory: it only resolves the observed modules and parent/operator references into Python closures and reads nothing from the fixture. No model parameters are transformed, packed or copied, no CUDA Graph is captured, no global torch backend/math flag is touched (evaluator's math_policy check stays green), and nothing is cached across invocations: every call recomputes the stem from its live input. Per-chunk temporaries (25.69 MB conv/BN/ReLU outputs, 6.42 MB pooled chunk, 12.84 MB int64 pool indices) and the single 25.69 MB output tensor are allocated inside each invocation through the caching allocator, so after the warmup invocations they are served from cached blocks; the setup receipt's allocated_bytes after installation remains the prepared model + pixels exactly as the parent. Retained allocator pools may come to include the 25.69/12.84 MB block classes used by the chunked path (framework.reserved/lifecycle counters can differ from the parent), while the objective framework.peak_allocated_bytes is reset per invocation and reflects only live allocations; the predicted decrease is specific to the warm-run peak_allocated_bytes counter of this workload, not a general physical-memory saving.
quality_risks: Chunked conv2d runs cudnn's heuristic at batch 8 instead of batch 32 (cudnn.benchmark stays False). For this 3->64 7x7 stride-2 convolution the implicit-GEMM family accumulates each output element over the same 147-element reduction independently of the batch dimension, so per-sample results are expected to be bitwise identical (verified bitwise-exact for the per-sample operators in CPU plumbing tests); if a different algorithm were selected, per-element differences are fp32 round-off (~1e-6 relative), far below the frozen logits tolerance atol=rtol=1e-4 and immaterial to argmax margins, but this is the one numerics uncertainty and is left to the frozen evaluator's closeness, exact-top1 and +1-corruption checks.

Latency floor risk: ~15 extra host launches (hidden by the observed ~2 ms host slack) and ~51 MB of extra D2D copy traffic (~60-170 us depending on achieved copy bandwidth) against the 224.7 us budget; if a chunked cudnn algorithm were slower the chunk size is retunable inside the same boundary without changing the frozen semantics.

The four aten sites now execute with chunk-shaped signatures through context['references']; on the next discovery recapture they will be re-keyed under new call ids with the chunk signature (the framework recaptures the plan; consumers of the stem output still receive a contiguous (32,64,56,56) fp32 CUDA tensor exactly as the parent pooler produced).

Fallback labels keep the failure taxonomy observable: 'setup_failure_parent' (unresolved modules/references), 'unsupported_signature_parent' (guard mismatch, e.g. training mode, non-fp32/CPU tensors, non-zeros padding, grouped conv, indices/ceil_mode pooling), 'runtime_failure_parent' (operator exception mid-composite, full parent recompute). The framework's signature guard additionally only dispatches the observed (32,3,224,224) call to the replacement at all.
proposal.eliminated_calls_rationale: The whole stem bundle inside model.resnet.embedder is replaced at its boundary, so the inner Python module calls no longer execute as module calls: ResNetConvLayer (fad32b28bd6e0def6ce7593e), Conv2d (a929588cc0791799075542c6), BatchNorm2d (d2690ee924ab33cd95efa6f0), ReLU (9bb381a7b50f1e3dcfdb1cb4) and MaxPool2d (12da68be9b9e14502fe4702a). Their computational content is preserved exactly: the replacement reads the same live module parameters (conv weight/stride/padding, BN affine and running stats, pool geometry) and executes the equivalent aten operators through context['references'] on every invocation; only the intermediate Python module boundaries and the full-resolution temporaries they materialized are gone. The only consumer of these calls' outputs is the stem itself, which returns the same contiguous (32,64,56,56) fp32 CUDA tensor to the encoder stages, so all downstream consumers remain valid. The profiler record_function enter/exit sites (1f750cfe73af31647514bce9, 5a738567860d1790e17b4c74, 74a7d1dc7c252585bac9ee72, 9beb8b9076cc061fb8023ead, 9d3d81c3c57605e001aa0979, a263d10c24fce1ff47e60d76, b04ed2ee2118d432096eebe4) are discovery instrumentation markers around the captured ops, not computational work; their consumers are trace analysis only, and the framework's recapture will emit fresh markers for the chunked path.

State lifecycle and synchronization: single process on one CUDA device, single stream, no collectives, nothing cached across invocations, no model parameters transformed, packed or copied; each invocation recomputes both stages from the live input tensor, reset()/models() semantics are untouched, and the returned tensors are freshly allocated contiguous fp32 CUDA tensors with the parent's exact shapes, so downstream stages and the classifier head remain valid consumers. stages.2/stages.3 stay deliberately outside the boundary: their eager moments (~104-111 MB) already sit below the post-edit floor set by the chunked stages.0 moment, so replacing them would add eliminated-call surface and launch overhead without moving the objective.
proposal.setup_work: build(context) performs no GPU work and allocates no device memory: it resolves the two stage parent callables from context['references'], the conv/batch-norm/relu/identity/shortcut modules from context['modules'] and the 30 aten operator references into Python closures, and verifies module types (Conv2d, BatchNorm2d with affine+running stats, out-of-place ReLU, Identity tails/shortcuts) once at installation; any mismatch only clears the ready flag so calls fall back to the parent under the setup_failure_parent label. No model parameters are transformed, packed or copied, no CUDA Graph is captured, no global torch backend/math flag is touched (the evaluator's math_policy check stays green), and nothing is cached across invocations. Per-chunk temporaries (two to three 6,422,528 B (8,64,56,56) tensors in stages.0, up to five 3,211,264 B (8,128,28,28) tensors in stages.1) and the single preallocated full-size stage outputs (25,690,112 B and 12,845,056 B) are allocated inside each invocation through the caching allocator, so after warmup they are served from cached blocks and the setup receipt's allocated_bytes after installation remains the prepared model + pixels exactly as the parent. Retained allocator pools may come to include the 6.42/3.21 MB chunk block classes, so framework.reserved_bytes and the lifecycle peak counters can differ from the parent, while the objective framework.peak_allocated_bytes is reset per invocation and reflects only live allocations; the predicted decrease is specific to the warm-run peak_allocated_bytes counter of this workload, not a general physical-memory saving. The chunk size is read once from context['parameters']['chunk_samples'] (default 8; any non-positive or non-int value falls back to 8) and is fixed for the bundle installation.
quality_risks: Chunked conv2d runs cudnn's heuristic at the chunk batch size instead of batch 32 (cudnn.benchmark stays False). The implicit-GEMM family accumulates each output element over the same 3-tap or 9-tap reduction independently of the batch dimension, and the accepted stem bundle measured bitwise-identical logits (max_abs_error 0.0) with the same chunking; if a different algorithm were selected at stages.1's winograd-friendly shapes, per-element differences are fp32 round-off (~1e-6 relative), far below the frozen logits tolerance atol=rtol=1e-4 and immaterial to argmax margins. This remains the one numerics uncertainty and is left to the frozen evaluator's closeness, exact-top1 and +1-corruption checks.

Latency floor risk: ~38.5 MB of extra D2D copy traffic (~85 us), ~140 extra host launches (absorbed by the observed ~2 ms host dispatch slack) and possibly +18% conv time at batch-8 chunk shapes, partially offset by the measured ~3x speedup of the BN/relu kernels at smaller batch, against ~460 us of headroom on the 4.4942 ms floor; the chunk_samples parameter (4/8/16) is retunable by the frozen search inside the same boundary without changing semantics.

The 30 aten sites now execute with chunk-shaped signatures through context['references']; on the next discovery recapture they will be re-keyed under new call ids with chunk signatures (the framework recaptures the plan); consumers of the stage outputs still receive contiguous (32,64,56,56)/(32,128,28,28) fp32 CUDA tensors exactly as the parent produced.

Fallback labels keep the failure taxonomy observable: 'setup_failure_parent' (unresolved modules/references or module-type mismatch, including a replaced layer's shortcut no longer being Identity/conv+bn as assumed), 'unsupported_signature_parent' (guard mismatch, e.g. training mode, non-fp32/non-CUDA/non-contiguous tensors, wrong channel count, non-zeros padding, grouped conv) and 'runtime_failure_parent' (operator exception mid-composite, full parent recompute on the original input). The framework's signature guard additionally only dispatches the observed (32,64,56,56) stage calls to the replacements at all.

Memory accounting risk: the preallocated full-size stage output makes the new stages.0 moment (~136.7 MB) the expected peak, but allocator behavior (block reuse for the 25.69 MB input/output classes versus the retired full-size temporaries) can shift the measured counter a few MB in either direction; reserved pools may grow even as the per-invocation allocated peak falls, which is expected and not part of the objective.

proposal.setup_work: build(context) performs no GPU work and allocates no device memory: it resolves the parent callable for fb7277dba44d770ed1cbb22f from context['references'], the ResNetModel module from context['modules'] (falling back to context['models']['model'].resnet), the 47 aten operator references from the current plan, and traverses the live module tree (embedder conv/bn/relu + MaxPool2d, the four stages with two basic layers each, per-layer conv/bn/ReLU/Identity/shortcut specs, the AdaptiveAvgPool2d pooler), verifying types, fp32 CUDA weights, eval mode, affine BatchNorm2d with running stats, non-inplace ReLU, groups=1, zeros padding mode and the pinned (in,out,kernel,stride) signature of every mapped conv once at installation; any mismatch only clears the ready flag so calls fall back to the parent under the setup_failure_parent label. No model parameters are transformed, packed or copied, no CUDA Graph is captured, no global torch backend/math flag is touched (the evaluator's math_policy check stays green), and nothing is cached across invocations; weights and BN statistics are read live from the module objects on every call, so the warm-model lifecycle (reset() reseeding and re-asserting eval, observe()'s repeated forward) sees consistent behavior. All streaming buffers - the per-stage-chunk stem assembly buffer (6,422,528 B at stage_samples=8), the macro stage-1 buffer (12,845,056 B at tail_samples=32), the preallocated (32,512,7,7) last_hidden_state (3,211,264 B) and (32,512,1,1) pooler_output (65,536 B), and the chunk-shaped conv/bn/relu temporaries - are allocated inside each invocation through the caching allocator and dropped promptly (explicit reference clears) once consumed, so after warmup they are served from cached blocks and the setup receipt's allocated_bytes after installation remains the prepared model + pixels exactly as the parent (previous receipts: 67,935,232 B). Retained allocator pools may come to include the 12.85/6.42/3.21 MB block classes, so framework.reserved_bytes and the lifecycle peak counters can differ from the parent even as the objective framework.peak_allocated_bytes - reset for each run - falls; the predicted decrease is specific to the warm-run peak_allocated_bytes counter of this workload, not a general physical-memory saving. The three chunk sizes are read once from context['parameters'] at build (defaults stem_samples=4, stage_samples=8, tail_samples=32; any non-positive or non-int value falls back to its default) and are fixed for the bundle installation.
quality_risks: cudnn algorithm selection at the new chunk shapes: the stem conv2d runs at batch 4 (default) instead of the parent's batch 8, and at tail_samples=16 the stages.2/3 convs run at batch 16 instead of 32 (cudnn.benchmark stays False, so heuristics pick per-shape algorithms; the diagnostic trace shows the full-batch stages.2/3 3x3 convs use winograd tile-generation kernels whose per-invocation overhead scales with chunk count). Per-element differences are fp32 round-off at the scale the accepted chunked bundles already measured (max_abs_error 7.63e-06), far below the frozen logits tolerance atol=rtol=1e-4 and immaterial to argmax margins; the frozen evaluator's closeness, exact-top1 and +1-corruption checks decide.

Throughput floor risk (images_per_second >= 7120.308, latency <= 4.4942 ms vs the parent's 4.2279 ms median with ~0.27 ms headroom): the defaults add roughly +20 aten-level calls (16 stem ops from 4-sample stem chunks plus finer plumbing, minus the retired full-size prealloc copies) and the stem conv runs at batch 4; the aggressive parameter points add more (tail_samples=16 adds ~31 stages.2/3 site invocations plus doubled winograd tile-generation; stem_samples=2 adds another 16 stem ops). stage_samples=4 is deliberately excluded because the previous sweep measured that exact failure mode (5,418.94 ips, 30 stage sites x 8 small convs). If a parameter endpoint violates the floor it is an invalid endpoint, not a publication; the search retains (8,*,32) and (*,16,*) as faster points.

output_hidden_states=True is not materialized by the streaming path (full per-stage hidden states would require exactly the full-size intermediates being eliminated) and falls back to the parent callable under unsupported_signature_parent; the frozen workload never requests it (config output_hidden_states=False, adapter calls model(pixel_values=pixels) only), and return_dict=False is handled natively by returning (last_hidden_state, pooler_output).
